title: Collapse an empty carton flat on the stack of knocked-down cartons it lies on
instruction: Collapse the empty carton flat where it lies on the stack, and leave the stack in place.
context: Stockers and order fillers (SOC 53-7065, about 2.8 million US jobs, BLS) empty cartons all shift and break each one down for the cardboard bay or baler: with the flaps already cut off, the carton is racked over along its creases until it lies flat, and it goes on the stack of flats. A carton left standing takes the room of the whole backroom; one forced across the wrong creases tears and springs open, so the stack leans and slides. The same rack-over is how most households break down a delivery box for the recycling bin, so the act is familiar on sight. Done by a robot, it is a two-step judgement in force: push the carton over along its own creases (not across them) and stop before the stack moves.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) Stack, loose: three knocked-down cartons, each 508 (y) x 152 (x) x 6.4 mm (a 12 x 8 x 6 in carton flat, two layers of 3.2 mm board), 0.085 kg each, centred x 270 mm, y 0, on a fixed brown board 540 x 175 x 3 mm; the stack's top is 22.2 mm up. Friction 0.5 board on board (est). (2) Carton, loose: brown single-wall C-flute, 12 x 8 x 6 in (305 x 203 x 152 mm), flaps already cut off, 0.085 kg in all (0.55 kg per square metre of board). It lies on the stack's top on one long side with its open ends along x, so it stands as a four-panel sleeve 203 mm tall: two long panels (305 x 152 mm) underneath and on top, two short panels (203 x 152 mm) at its ends, 3.2 mm slabs. The underneath panel spans y -254 to +51 mm at x 270 mm, so the -y end panel stands at the stack's -y end. The four corners are creases: rotating joints about axes along x, each held by 0.01 N m of friction and stopped about 97 degrees either side of square. The manufacturer's glue joint is the one at the -y end: a 38 mm tab creased on the end panel's edge and glued flat to the underneath panel, so the sleeve is a closed loop with one degree of freedom. The panels pass through one another in the model, so the crease angles, not contact, say how folded it is. Racking the sleeve toward +y by pushing the -y end panel turns all four creases together; fully racked it is two layers, 6.4 mm thick and 516 mm long, lying along the stack. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the carton's four panels, its four crease angles, the three flats of the stack, and both grippers. Flat: every crease within 15 degrees of fully shut (interior angle 0) or fully open (180); the carton's thickness (highest point over lowest) 12 mm or less; its footprint within 540 mm (y) x 180 mm (x). On the stack: the footprint's centre within 60 mm of the stack's centre (top view) and the carton's lowest point within 6 mm of the stack's top. Offset: the same within 120 mm and 20 mm. Stack kept: no flat moved over 15 mm (top view) or 4 mm up, or turned over 8 degrees. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' fingers are 30 mm or more from the carton and every flat, and nothing moves over 1 mm or turns over 0.3 degrees. Score 0 if any flat moved over 40 mm or turned over 30 degrees at any step, and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 flat, on the stack, stack kept; 0.75 flat, offset, stack kept; 0.5 flat anywhere else (or stack moved 15 to 40 mm); 0.25 not flat but 110 mm tall or less; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, per condition: flat, an angle gauge at each crease and a straight rule on top; on the stack, a rule and a straight edge across the stack; stack kept, a pencil mark and a rule; hands off, a 30 mm spacer and video.
reset_notes: Lay the three flats on the board, centred, edges square. Lay the carton on its long side on top, the glue tab at the -y end, its underneath panel from y -254 to +51 mm, creases square. Replace a carton whose creases have gone limp; cartons are single use after about five trials.
fidelity: Rigid 3.2 mm slabs on four revolute joints, 0.01 N m friction each (est); real corrugated creases spring back. The glue joint is a tab fixed to the underneath panel that never peels. Panels pass through one another, so crease angles and the 12 mm thickness limit say flat. Board 0.55 kg/m2, friction 0.5, crease friction (est): measure by hanging a panel level from a spring scale. The stack's flats are single slabs. Flaps cut off (a box-cutter step is covered elsewhere).
